title: Everyone online is suddenly saying Obsidian is useless with Claude Code, and they're wrong
description:
Everyone online is suddenly calling Obsidian useless with Claude Code. They're wrong. They're just using it for the wrong thing.

Honest part first: Obsidian by itself does not change how Claude remembers anything. What changes Claude's memory is how you structure your folders, and you can do that with or without Obsidian. So if that's all you wanted, fair enough.

But here's what it actually buys you. When your vault is split into raw data, analyzed notes, and finished outputs, Claude gets a map of where everything lives. It stops grepping through thousands of files and goes straight to the right one, which is faster and cheaper.

And the biggest reason is you. Past a few hundred thousand files, you need to see that structure and navigate it yourself. Obsidian gives you that window. The terminal never will.

So no, Obsidian isn't overhyped. The pretty knowledge graphs are. The structure underneath them is the whole point.

Comment VAULT and I'll send you the folder structure I use.
